utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: A very good afternoon to you all. Mr. Registrar, call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-5/18-R77.3 in the contempt case of Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Let counsel appearing for Mr. Krstic introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am Tomislav Visnjic, attorney, and I am the counsel of Mr. Radislav Krstic in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krstic, can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Are you receiving the interpretation in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I hear it quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: We are convening today for the trial of Mr. Radislav Krstic, accused of one count of contempt. Before we proceed, we are obliged under Rule 73 bis (A) of the Tribunal Rules of Procedure and Evidence to proceed with the Pre-Trial Conference prior to the commencement of the trial. I must also state that Rule 77(E) provides that "the rules of procedure and evidence in Parts Four to Eight shall apply mutatis mutandis to the proceedings" under Rule 77. The Chamber has decided to prosecute the charge of contempt set out in the order in lieu of indictment against Mr. Krstic issued on the 27th of March, 2013, pursuant to Rule 77(D)(ii) of the Tribunal Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Mr. Krstic, the order in lieu of indictment charges you with one count of contempt for having refused to comply with the Chamber's subpoena of 23rd October 2012 and the addendum to the subpoena of 7th November 2012. The Chamber, satisfied that there were no medical reasons which amounted to good cause for you not to comply with the subpoena, found that there was sufficient reason to believe that you knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice and therefore may be in contempt of the Tribunal. At your initial appearance on April 4, 2013, you maintained your position that you were not willing to testify in the case of the Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic. Now, Mr. Krstic, I ask you once again whether you are willing to testify in the Karadzic case. If necessary, you may consult your counsel before answering the question. And if you prefer, we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I stand by my position. I simply want to protect my health. I never said that I did not want to testify. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I shall first go over some details about the conduct of the trial. Mr. Visnjic, at this stage I will ask whether the Defence will make an opening statement pursuant to Rule 84 and whether the accused wishes to make a statement pursuant to Rule 84 bis of the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We do not intend to make an opening statement, nor is General Krstic willing to make any statement pursuant to Rule 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, does the Defence intend to call any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we intend to call one witness and that is the expert witness Ana Najman whose report you received in our submission dated the 21st of May, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: How long do you expect your submissions would last?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the timing, we expect that during one session we should finish the whole procedure, so not more than one hour and a half. We shall try to be efficient and therefore a part of our arguments are prepared in a written form submitted as a special motion entitled "Krstic Brief on Hearing on 28 May 2013, Filed on 21 May 2013". So our arguments will be focused on one part of the problem that we believe we are faced with, and our final statement, if we make one, will also be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krstic, do you have any issues you would like to raise about the conditions of your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no issues or any problems that I would burden the Tribunal and Your Honours with. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber, Mr. Krstic, is cognisant of the fact that in the past you have consented to discussions related to your health condition in the Karadzic case taking place in public session. The Chamber is aware, however, that the report of Dr. Ana Najman in this case and the medical reports in the Karadzic case have all been filed confidentially. The Chamber would like to know, would you prefer that discussions related to your health take place in public or private?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may answer this question. In this case, as we would deal in detail with some aspects and elements of General Krstic's health, we would prefer if this part of the trial would be conducted in private or closed session, I suppose private session, for the simple reason that I believe that certain details are a part of the general's privacy and are not something that would suitably be discussed in a public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, following from this, what impact would this have on the filing of Dr. Najman's report?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Najman's report, we would suggest that it be admitted as a confidential document as well as the other five documents which we've prepared for admission in this particular trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The Chamber will now consider the issues raised in Krstic Brief for Hearing on 28 May 2013, filed on 21st May 2013, and state straight away that it has no difficulty as respects the word limit for the filing. As relief sought, the Defence invites the Chamber to enter a verdict of not guilty in relation to the order in lieu of an indictment on the basis that reasonable doubt exists as to whether Mr. Krstic could be expected to comply with the subpoena and addendum in circumstances where that may well impact his mental health. In the same breath and in the alternative, the Defence requests the Chamber to recuse itself in favour of an independent Chamber "so that this vital issue can be looked at afresh." The Chamber is of the opinion that the most appropriate course of action at this juncture would be for it to deal with the question of recusal. The Chamber must stress, however, that should the request for recusal be refused, this refusal must not in any way be construed as having any impact or bearing, one way or the other, on its ultimate decision on the charge of contempt. The well-established and settled jurisprudence of this Tribunal is that an act of contempt can be prosecuted by the Chamber hearing the proceedings in which the contempt arises, unless there are exceptional circumstances for the Chamber to recuse itself. The Chamber gave full consideration to the submission of the Defence and at the end of the day was unable to perceive any exceptional circumstance which could have warranted the Chamber recusing itself in this matter. The request is accordingly denied. Now, in line with the Chamber's Scheduling Order for commencement of the trial dated 7th May 2013 and since there are no additional pending issues before the Chamber, we may now proceed with the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: We shall now commence the trial. Now, before hearing the Defence, the Chamber will now give a summary of the case against Mr. Krstic. On the 23rd of October, 2012, the Chamber in the Karadzic case granted a motion by Radovan Karadzic issuing a subpoena ordering Mr. Krstic to appear and testify in the Karadzic case on 15 January 2013 or to show good cause why the subpoena could not be complied with. On 7th November 2012 the Chamber issued an addendum to the subpoena, ordering that the appearance and testimony of Mr. Krstic be postponed until 4th February 2013 or that good cause be shown as to why the subpoena should not be complied with. On 6 February 2013 Mr. Krstic, through his counsel, filed a confidential motion arguing that for medical reasons he does not have the capacity to testify, and requesting that the Chamber stay the enforcement of the subpoena "until such time as a further medical review can be completed to assess the medical and mental health conditions of the witness as well as his ability, capacity, and competence to testify." On 7 February 2013 the Chamber denied the urgent motion and held that Mr. Krstic's mental and physical health is such that he is able to testify. On 7 February 2013 Mr. Krstic refused to testify and the Chamber heard further submissions as to why he believed he could not testify. The Chamber then ordered that the Registry provide by 8 March 2013 a more detailed report outlining Mr. Krstic's physical and mental health. On 14 February 2013 the Tribunal's Deputy Registrar appointed an independent medical expert to conduct the examination. On 13 March 2013, having reviewed the medical report filed on 8 March, the Chamber found that there were no medical reasons which would amount to good cause for Mr. Krstic not to comply with the subpoena. Accordingly, the subpoena ordered that Mr. Krstic -- that the Chamber ordered that Mr. Krstic comply with the subpoena and reminded him that failure to do so would constitute contempt of the Tribunal pursuant to Rule 77 of the Rules. On 19 March 2013 Mr. Krstic, through his counsel, filed confidentially Krstic's request for reconsideration of the order dated 13 March 2013, requesting that the Chamber reconsider its decision of 13 March 2013 because Mr. Krstic was not given the opportunity to make submissions as to the meaning and impact of the medical report. On 21st March 2013 the Chamber found that Mr. Krstic did not meet the test for reconsideration. On 22nd March 2013, the Chamber received a confidential "Letter from Radislav Krstic to Trial Chamber" reiterating his refusal to testify before the Chamber. On 22nd March 2013 the Chamber ordered that Mr. Krstic appear before it on 25th March 2013. On 25th March 2013 Mr. Krstic appeared before the Chamber and persisted in his refusal to testify. On 27 March 2013 an order in lieu of indictment was issued. As stated earlier, Mr. Krstic is being prosecuted for contempt for having knowingly and willingly interfered with the administration of justice by refusing to comply with this subpoena. Mr. Krstic, at this point you may lead the Defence. Mr. Visnjic, I do apologise most profoundly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before we call our first witness, perhaps I should provide an explanation to the Trial Chamber of certain documents that we have tendered as exhibits in e-court and which are cited in our submission of the 21st of May, 2013. The first document is 1D1 and it is called -- or rather, it's 1D1 and it's called -- actually, it's a medical file, I'm sorry. And within that file there is a document cited in our letter in paragraph 6. It is referred to as the Lefrandt report and it's to be found on pages 7, 8, and 9 of the medical file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, would you want to give this report a separate number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I only wish to make it clear that within a rather voluminous medical file, what are the references and where they can be found from our brief. Then document 1D2 is a document mentioned in paragraph 12 of our brief as well as footnote 11. The document 1D3 in e-court is referred to in paragraph 13 of our brief and footnote 11. The document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, may I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, can you give me, as you mentioned, some idea what the report is, from which doctor? Now, ID2 is in respect to which doctor?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2 is a letter, or rather, it's the request for medical documentation. It's the letter that I sent to the UNDU, the commanding officer, on the 3rd of January, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, 1D3 is Dr. E. van Gellicum's report. The document 1D4 is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, at this point would you prefer that we go into private session or are you happy right now being in public?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. For as long as I'm referring to the documents, their contents are confidential but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Very well. So the report of Dr. Gellicum, 1D3 you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is 1D3, yes. 1D4 is Dr. De Man's expert report or variously referred to as the De Man report mentioned in paragraphs 20 through 23 of our brief, and 1D5 is Najman's report referred to in paragraph 37 of our brief. I hope that this will be of assistance to the Trial Chamber to find their way through the documentation that we are partly to blame for having uploaded at this late stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, the reports of Dr. Petrovic, would you be referring to them at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is part of document 1D1. It's part of the medical file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: This is in the medical documentation? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's pages 10 through 14 or through to the end actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now, we observed that the CV of Dr. Najman was not uploaded. Would you want to have this admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Frankly, we have neglected to do that. Perhaps we may upload it at a later date, but that's part of our filing of the 21st of May, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I shall be grateful for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now that we are on this issue, unless there are any other technical issues, I would like to call our first and only witness, Ana Najman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: We would have the Registrar apportion the various numbers to the various exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter numbers 1D1 through 1D5 will be Exhibits D1 to D5, all under seal and confidential. And the CV of Dr. Najman will be Exhibit D6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Also under seal? Also under seal, Dr. Najman's report?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Dr. Najman's report will be under seal. The CV will be public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to call our only witness, Ana Najman, specialist in psychology and court expert, permanent court expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Do take the solemn affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Dr. Najman.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Your CV has already been admitted into evidence in this case and I will only have one question to do with your CV which actually may add to it. You have also testified before the Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in how many cases did you testify and at whose invitation?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, let me say that I was called by the Chamber, although on several occasions I was called by the Defence. And the exact number, it's difficult for me to be precise. Around ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, your report is called "Psychological Expert Examination, Expert Report on Psychological Assessment." What does "psychological expert examination" really mean?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, it consists of a psycho-diagnostic interview conducted with the interviewee which is followed by a series of psychological tests. The tests are chosen depending on the diagnostic assessment arrived at -- the diagnostic assessment as a result of the interview conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the difference is between psychological and psychiatric expert examination?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: As I've said, psychological expert assessment implies the application of a series of standardised psychological tests intended to assess the structure and dynamics of a personality, intellectual capacities, mental deficits or deficiencies, if any. Now, the psychiatric examination will mostly include a psychiatric interview and, at times, the application of certain many scales for the assessment of the interviewee's condition as well as focusing on clinical symptoms that may arise in the context of a certain disorder or condition. Therefore, the crucial difference lies in the fact that a psychologist, a clinical psychologist, will use a set of valid and verified psychological tests, whereas a psychiatrist will not be using such a valid objectivised series of tests.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report it is stated that you used certain psychological techniques. Some of them were provided as tables in the addendum. Now, the question is: Why exactly these techniques and which of the techniques that you used did you actually provide in the annex?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I was guided by the assignment that I was given with regard to the assessment of Mr. Krstic. In addition, there is a statistical protocol dictated by our profession which will help us assess the structure and dynamics of a personality. Now, it is, in fact, an obligatory practice, and this is something that we need to use is the projective test. And in 99.9 per cent of cases it's the Rorschach Projective Personality Test that has to be used, which I used. And questionnaires are used, two or maybe even three, as many as necessary, in order to arrive at a psychological diagnosis in terms of the personality structure and emergent disorder.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you conducted several tests and you applied several techniques. Is it necessary for similar results to occur at all the tests or most of the tests in order to be able to come to a conclusion, or is it possible to have some divergences there?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, in psychological diagnosis you have to assess the results of the tests. In layman's terms, everything has to be in agreement, everything has to fit in. The data that you obtained through the interview has to be confirmed by the projective techniques and the questionnaires that you also used. In most cases the psychologist will never use just one test because that would be unprofessional and would not yield valid results. But in psychology there is the configural approach, as we call it, which means that we have to produce a compact picture where everything is linked with everything else in order to be able to say this person has a personality structure of this or that kind or that the disorders are of this or that nature. And using the interview and projective techniques, and indeed the questionnaires - this is indeed what I have done - we come to this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we will be dealing with some quite specific results from the expert report, and I would like to ask us to go into private session. Just to let the audience know, it will probably -- we will probably have to be in private session for the whole duration of Dr. Najman's testimony. So perhaps they should be apprised of the fact that we will be proceeding in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: For the benefit of the members of the public in the public galleries, we shall be moving into private session and it could be that we might be there for some time during the course of this -- the evidence of this witness. Thank you. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And you're relieved. Thank you very much indeed, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no other documents to submit except for Dr. Najman's report to be admitted. I'm willing to give brief closing arguments which would not last more than ten minutes, unless there are any other requests on the part of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, unfortunately, I believe that a part of my closing arguments will deal with General Krstic's health and as it is brief I suggest that perhaps we should continue with that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Let me know when you want to switch over. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, this trial opened some ethical and legal issues, the answers to which are sometimes easy and sometimes difficult to give. In an ideal world it would be easy to separate personal and general interest and favour general interest rather than personal interest. In the real world it is not always so. General Krstic's case is one such case, as we deeply believe. This trial boils down to two simple questions: Firstly, whether by testifying in the Radovan Karadzic case General Krstic will jeopardise his health. Our answer is yes. And the other issue: Is the general interest such that this threatening of his health would be justified? We believe that the answer to the second question is negative. As for the first question, in our motion filed on the 21st of May, 2013, especially in paragraphs 6 to 25 as well as in today's proceedings through Dr. Najman's testimony, we provided a series of evidence showing that the degree of threat to General Krstic's health is such that his testimony in this case would, with a very high likelihood, cause permanent effects which would mean a deterioration of his health with a prognosis that it would be very difficult to treat him fully considering the conditions under which he would be treated. General Krstic is faced with a dilemma, a threat with a short prison sentence due to contempt of court or anxiety, depression, nightmares, flashbacks, and fear that would extend for a period of years. Is that a reasonable justification or a good reason? We believe it is. As for the second question that the Chamber could try to assess -- and perhaps we could now move into private session because I'm not sure if this segment of my speech is confidential or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And we shall deliver our judgement at a date to be announced. The hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.40 p.m.
